title: Model ecosystem adoption playbook + competitor pricing & signals snapshot
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Objective: produce a concise, actionable playbook that translates model-ecosystem adoption signals into sales/PM recommendations and a competitive pricing snapshot for GTM.

Scope: 1) Track adoption signals (open-source forks, huggingface downloads, GitHub stars/activity, cloud infra availability) for 12 prioritized models. 2) Map each model to commercial risk vectors (license, quantization maturity, operator ecosystems). 3) Produce a competitor pricing snapshot (hosted/per-token, dedicated capacity equivalents, latency SLAs) for 6 vendors. 4) Deliver a one-page playbook for Sales/SEs outlining when to position Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private based on adoption/price/latency.

Out-of-scope: deep model quality evals (separate evals squad), full legal license review (legal to be consulted for flagged items).
acceptance_criteria: 12-model tracker populated with 6 adoption signals each (downloads, GitHub activity, upstream community forks, cloud AMIs, public benchmarks, model card maturity)
Competitive pricing table with normalized cost-per-1k-token and a dedicated-capacity equivalent estimate for 6 vendors
Playbook one-pager (PDF) with 3 routing heuristics: cost-first, latency-first, compliance-first
Sales enablement deck (5 slides) and 2 example rebuttals for common competitor claims
Hand-off to Solutions: two 30-min walkthrough sessions scheduled and recording uploaded
activity: 2026-01-18 — Kickoff: aligned with GTM, Research, and Eng leads. Prioritized 12 models: LlamaX-70B, OpenAlly-30B, Falcon-Refined, Mosaic-M, MetaOpen-34B, TitanLite, StableLM-2, Baize-Chat, Vicuna-13B, Mistral-Instruct, Cerebras-7B, Obsidian-Base.
2026-01-20 — Research: scraped initial adoption metrics (HuggingFace downloads, GH stars). Noted Falcon-Refined has a rapid increase in forks; flagged for licensing check.
2026-01-22 — PM/Eng sync: Eng to estimate Dedicated-equivalent throughput for each model (ENG-3082). Decided to use 1k-token normalized benchmark at 512 context for pricing parity.
2026-01-25 — Drafted competitor pricing normalization method. Feedback from Finance: include reserved vs burst assumptions and include amortized GPU cost for Dedicated equivalents.
2026-01-28 — Draft playbook outline completed. Sales requested two short rebuttals emphasizing fallback routing and cost transparency features.
2026-01-30 — Design reviewed one-pager layout; requested callouts for SLO examples and a small decision tree. (Design to provide assets: DES-214)
2026-02-01 — Legal intake: submitted license fingerprint list for 3 models (follow-up needed for Falcon-Refined; legal-ticket created).
2026-02-02 — Status: core tracker 85% complete, competitive pricing table 60% complete, playbook first draft ready for internal review. Scheduled Solutions walkthrough for 2026-02-04.
notes: Normalization rules: convert hosted price to $/1k tokens using vendor published rates; for dedicated, compute equivalent hourly GPU cost and map to tokens using our 512-token amortization baseline
Adoption signals prioritized: community growth > infra availability > published benchmarks > dataset reuse
Immediate risks: licensing ambiguity for forks, rapid community forks making signal noisy — recommend weekly refresh for next 8 weeks
Follow-ups: request ENG-3082 throughput estimates by 2026-02-04; Solutions walkthrough recording to be stored in attachments
